# 046 — ItemList + Dataset JSON-LD on token/chain pool tables

Risk tier: **HIGH** (verifier-confirmed, agrees with the builder's guess). Full walkthrough below, per NORTH_STAR's HIGH-lane requirement.

## Goal
Every `/tokens/<slug>` and `/chains/<slug>` page's core content — a ranked table of live pools by TVL — carried zero structured data before this change. 040 shipped `Organization`/`WebSite`/`BreadcrumbList`/`FAQPage` for the site's identity and navigation, but deliberately left the pages' actual ranked data invisible to structured-data consumers (search rich results, AI-answer citation crawlers). This closes that gap with `ItemList` (the ranked pools) and `Dataset` (the yields dataset the page presents) — additive only, no visible/canonical/ranking/trust-rail change.

## Intuition
Two schema.org types, for two different questions a crawler might ask about the page:
- **"What's the ranked list on this page?"** → `ItemList`. Google's own carousel/rich-result guidance is explicit that a page listing several items should mark that list up as `ItemList`, and — just as importantly — that mis-typing something like an APY as a `Product`'s `price` risks a manual action for misleading structured data. 040 already made that call for individual pools (deferred `Product`/`FinancialProduct`); this diff makes the *safe* version of the same idea real: the list itself, not each item as a priced product.
- **"What data underlies this page?"** → `Dataset`. The page is fundamentally presenting a live yields dataset filtered through DeFi Garden's trust rails; `Dataset` says that honestly (name, description, who publishes it, when it was last generated) without claiming anything about individual pools that isn't already said elsewhere.

The one design decision worth calling out: rather than compute the `ItemList` items separately and hope they stay in sync with the visible `<tr>` rows, both now flow through the *same* function (`poolHrefFor`) over the *same* array (`rec.pools`) in the *same* order. Google's structured-data policy requires the schema to reflect visible content — this diff doesn't just test that invariant, it makes violating it require editing two call sites to disagree with each other, which is a much higher bar than a passing test alone.

## What changed and why (diff in reading order)

**`generate-token-pages.js`** (the shared module `generate-chain-pages.js` reuses):
1. `poolHrefFor(p, fallbackUrl)` — pulled the existing inline `p.pool ? /?pool=<id> : fallbackUrl` logic out of the row-rendering closure into a named, exported, reusable function. No behavior change yet — this step alone is a pure refactor that both the table row and the new JSON-LD will call.
2. `renderItemListJsonLd(pools, appUrl)` — builds `{ "@type": "ItemList", itemListElement: [...] }` from the given `pools` array, `position` = index+1, `name` = `"<project> on <chain>"`, `url` = `poolHrefFor(p, appUrl)`. Same `</`-escaping as the existing `breadcrumbJsonLd` (prevents a malicious `project`/`chain` string from breaking out of the `<script>` tag).
3. `renderDatasetJsonLd(name, description, pageUrl, generatedDate)` — generic Dataset block; `creator`/`publisher` both resolve to a `DeFi Garden` `Organization` object matching 040's site identity.
4. `renderTokenPage(rec, related, generatedDate)` — added the third param (optional, defaults to today's date). After the existing `breadcrumbJsonLd` construction, builds `itemListJsonLd` (from `rec.pools` + the page's own `appUrl`) and `datasetJsonLd` (name/description built from `rec.symbol`). The row-rendering `poolHref` line now calls `poolHrefFor(p, appUrl)` instead of repeating the inline ternary — same output, now provably shared with the JSON-LD. Two new `<script type="application/ld+json">` tags inserted in `<head>` immediately after the BreadcrumbList one.
5. `module.exports` — added `poolHrefFor`, `renderItemListJsonLd`, `renderDatasetJsonLd` so `generate-chain-pages.js` can reuse them (CLAUDE.md's reuse-before-inventing rule — chain pages already import several token-page helpers this same way).

**`generate-chain-pages.js`**:
1. Destructures the three new exports from `tp` (the token-pages module) alongside its existing imports.
2. `renderChainPage(rec, related, generatedDate)` — identical shape of change to `renderTokenPage`: builds `itemListJsonLd` from `rec.pools` + `appUrl`, `datasetJsonLd` from `rec.chain`, inserts both `<script>` tags after the breadcrumb, and the row loop now calls the shared `poolHrefFor` instead of its own inline copy.

**`test_token_pages.js` / `test_chain_pages.js`**: a new `"046 — ItemList + Dataset JSON-LD"` section in each, mirroring 040's existing BreadcrumbList test structure — see the Test plan section of the PR description for exactly what's asserted.

**`product-loop-kit/specs/046-notes.md`**: build notes — deviations, the manual Rich-Results property checklist (no live Google tool available in-sandbox, same fallback 040 used), and the full test-run record.

## Deviations from spec
See `product-loop-kit/specs/046-notes.md` for the full reasoning; summary:
- `Dataset.dateModified` uses the CI generation-time date (048's freshness work hasn't shipped yet) via a new optional `generatedDate` param — a clean hook for 048 to wire into later, not a blocker now.
- Chain-page `ItemList.name` uses the identical `"<project> on <chain>"` format as token pages (a touch redundant since every chain-page pool is already on that chain) — a conscious choice to keep one shared, provably-correct function rather than two near-duplicate implementations.
- No live Google Rich Results Test available in this sandbox — substituted the same manual property-checklist approach 040 used.

## Verifier outcome
PASS, HIGH tier (agrees with builder's guess). Verifier independently regenerated fixture output pre/post-diff and confirmed byte-for-byte that only the two new `<script>` tags were added; ran `test_token_pages.js` (51/51), `test_chain_pages.js` (45/45), the NORTH_STAR canonical test command (190 assertions), plus `test_canonical.js`/`test_hub_pages.js`/`test_indexnow.js`/`test_stories.js` — all green.
